title: Mark Zuckerberg & T-Pain Celebrate 10 Years of Smokin' Meats
htmlContent:
Some anniversaries call for cake. Mark Zuckerberg's called for ribs. The Meta CEO went live on Instagram today to mark exactly ten years since his original Smoking Meats broadcast, the 2016 stream that turned a backyard cook into one of the internet's most durable memes. Smokin' Meats v2 just dropped, and it came with a surprise guest: T-Pain, who hopped on the live to send his congratulations from what looked like a garage full of fast cars.

A Decade-Old Meme Gets a Sequel

Back in 2016, Instagram Live was still finding its footing, and the sight of one of the most powerful people in tech earnestly tending a smoker became instant internet folklore. The phrase "smoking meats" took on a life of its own, showing up in memes, reaction clips, and running jokes about Zuckerberg's attempts to seem relatable. For years, it was the kind of moment people brought up to poke a little fun.

Ten years later, Zuckerberg is in on the joke. Rather than letting the anniversary pass quietly, he leaned all the way in, firing up the smoker once again and inviting the internet back to the grill. This time, though, he showed up prepared.

T-Pain Pulls Up With the Boys

The most energetic moment of the stream came when T-Painjoined the live. The Grammy-winning artist, known as much for his car obsession as for his music, popped in surrounded by friends and machines.

"We're out here with the boys. I got Herc here," T-Pain said, before turning the camera. "Herc, say what's up to the boys."

After a quick "What's up?" from Herc, T-Pain got straight to business.

"Oh, yeah. Yeah, we gotta go drifting, Mark."

Zuckerberg took it in stride.

"Whoa. Alright, have fun. I'll come join you sometime."

T-Pain wasn't about to let that slide as a polite brush-off.

"We gotta do. We got enough cars for you, man. We're ready to go."

Zuckerberg, clearly impressed by the lineup behind him, replied:

"Yeah, look at those whips. Oh, man."

An Invitation to Kauai

The drifting talk quickly turned into a standing invitation. T-Pain reminded Zuckerberg of an earlier offer.

"You told me to come out to Hawaii to start."

Zuckerberg confirmed it.

"Yeah, no, you gotta come drift at our track in Kauai," he said, describing a small setup on his Hawaiian property.

T-Pain had his answer ready.

"We got some cars ready to go."

It was a loose, unscripted exchange, the kind that makes live video work. Two people from very different worlds, bonding over horsepower and tire smoke while a different kind of smoke rolled off the grill.

Ranch-to-Grill: Ribs and Hot Dogs From Kauai

If the 2016 broadcast was about a man and his meat, the 2026 edition was about a man, his meat, and where it came from. Zuckerberg cooked ribs alongside hot dogs sourced from his own ranch in Kauai, where he raises his own livestock.

That detail gives the sequel a different flavor from the original. A decade ago, the cook was the whole story. Now the menu is a farm-to-table project, with the CEO overseeing the process from pasture to plate. It is a fitting evolution for someone whose public persona has shifted over the years from awkward hoodie-wearing founder to martial artist, surfer, and rancher.

The Muse Agent Takes Over the Smoker

The biggest upgrade from 2016 was not the meat. It was the setup. Zuckerberg revealed during the live that his Muse AI agent — Meta's new personal AI assistant unveiled at Connect last month — is now connected to his smoker via Bluetooth and can monitor the cook remotely.

He mentioned multiple times that his Muse agent was essentially watching the meat so he didn't have to. Temperature checks, timing, and the long hours of babysitting that serious barbecue demands were handed off to an AI.

For Meta, it was a clever bit of product placement wrapped in a nostalgia trip. Rather than demoing Muse on a stage with slides and charts, Zuckerberg showed it doing something ordinary and relatable: keeping an eye on dinner. A decade later, the meats are literally smoking themselves.

Why the Anniversary Landed

Part of what made the stream work was its self-awareness. Zuckerberg could have treated the original Smoking Meats video as an embarrassing relic. Instead, he turned it into a tradition, complete with a celebrity cameo and a tech showcase. The callback rewarded longtime internet watchers who remember the original while giving newcomers a glimpse of where Meta's AI ambitions are headed.

T-Pain's appearance added genuine warmth. His car culture and Zuckerberg's newer hobbies overlapped in an unexpectedly natural way, and the drifting invite gave the stream a storyline that could easily carry into a future video.

Here's to 10 More

Before signing off, T-Pain offered a heartfelt send-off.

"Congratulations on the 10-year anniversary, man. It's a really cool thing what you're doing, man, and you know, just hope you keep going, brother. I'm proud of you, man."

Zuckerberg returned the love.

"Thank you, dude. Thank you for including me in the anniversary." "And 10 more, man," T-Pain added. "10 more, dude."

If the next decade brings drifting in Kauai, a fully automated smoker, and another round of ribs, the internet will be watching. Smokin' Meats has officially become a franchise.
excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg marked exactly ten years since his original 2016 Smoking Meats Instagram Live with a sequel stream featuring a surprise appearance from T-Pain, ranch-raised ribs and hot dogs from Kauai, and a demo of Meta's new Muse AI agent monitoring the smoker via Bluetooth.
